projects.title: ChemPath
projects.description: A computational chemistry project that models organic reaction pathways as directed weighted graphs and explores shortest-path algorithms for navigating synthesis networks.
projects.longDescription: ChemPath is an independent computational chemistry project exploring whether organic synthesis pathways can be represented as directed weighted graphs and navigated using graph-theoretic algorithms. The current prototype implements a C++ reaction graph engine and Dijkstra's shortest-path algorithm, with future work planned around chemically informed heuristics, alternative pathfinding methods, and integration with MechLang for visualization.

projects.title: Motion Explainer
projects.description: An individual skill I developed within my fork of Anthropic's Skills repository. It creates animated, step-by-step visual explanations of concepts using p5.js, with support for interactive prediction, parameter sliders, misconception scenes, mathematical notation, and 2D/3D visualizations.
projects.longDescription: Motion Explainer is a reusable skill for turning concepts into animated visual narratives. It structures an explanation around a clear conceptual arc, then builds it as a sequence of scenes using a fixed viewer template. The skill supports p5.js animation, KaTeX-rendered mathematics, interactive prediction pauses, misconception scenes, parameter controls, responsive 2D or WEBGL rendering, and reusable animation and drawing primitives. The implementation lives specifically in the motion-explainer directory of my fork of Anthropic's Skills repository. The other skills in that fork are upstream Anthropic work and are not part of this project.

projects.title: MechLang
projects.description: MechLang explores a simple question: can chemistry be represented better than static diagrams? It is a domain-specific language for writing, understanding, and visualizing organic reaction mechanisms as structured code that both humans and computers can reason about.
projects.longDescription: MechLang is a domain-specific language designed to represent organic chemistry reaction mechanisms as structured, executable code — replacing static diagrams with a notation that both humans and computers can understand.
